text:
# Changelog

Notable changes, newest first. The Deploy pipeline refuses to release while
the Unreleased section is empty, and stamps it with the released version.

## Unreleased

This release adds action approvals, browser site permissions and network proxy settings, switches sessions to an append-only log, and fixes slowdowns when many sessions are open.

### New features

- **Action approvals** — Added Allow for this session and, in coding chats, Always allow to approval cards, revocable with "Ask again"; payments and permanent deletes always ask.
- **Browser site permissions** — Added default permissions and per-site exceptions under Settings › Authentication, with prompts that remember choices for a site, all sites, or until the app quits.
- **Chrome cookie auto-import** — Added under Settings › Authentication to re-import cookies on app start and Chrome close after one manual import with administrator approval, keeping Browser Use signed in.
- **Automatic verification codes** — Added automatic filling of one-time sign-in codes from your connected mailbox, plus phone prompts for passwords and codes.
- **Network proxy** — Added system, custom `http`/`https`/`socks5`, and off proxy modes with bypass rules and connection testing under Settings › System › Network proxy and phone settings, applying changes to the very next request across all providers (#317).

### Changes

- Changed sessions to save as an append-only log for faster, safer saving on close, converting existing sessions automatically in the background on first launch while keeping the original files and showing conversion status in `/doctor`.
- Changed browser actions to click through steps directly and try existing sessions or saved logins first, handing off only passwords, cards, codes, or identity checks.
- Changed the Android app to show a reconnect screen, reconnect automatically when the network returns or the app reopens, and offer "Choose another PC".
- Changed worktree removal to delete a branch only when Mixdog created it and git considers it merged, keeping its commits recoverable.
- Changed the support address to support@mixdog.ai and the website link to mixdog.ai.

### Bug fixes

- Fixed the app slowing down or stalling with many open sessions, and sped up opening sessions after launch (#316).
- Fixed Computer Use clicks missing targets on scaled high-DPI displays, background actions pulling focus and flickering the active window, and your own mouse or keyboard input pausing every agent instead of only the one it interrupted, which now resumes when you're idle or with Resume (#323).
- Fixed worker and sub-agent status to show the real state from start to finish and count hidden thinking as progress, so working agents are no longer treated as stalled (#319).
- Fixed reset-ticket details in the usage popup to expand in place so every ticket's expiry stays readable (#324).
- Fixed the live status line under a running turn overlapping its text in narrow windows during a long wait (#326).
- Fixed the window frame flickering to its inactive look when focus moves to another window or back on Windows Mica.
- Fixed a full disk shutting down the background service instead of retrying saves and still delivering shell results.
- Fixed `/stop` on shell jobs to report jobs that had already finished instead of "Couldn't stop" and free the project folder right away.
- Fixed the phone app waiting on large content when opening side panels, clipping values in the route editor model menu, disconnecting after a single missed acknowledgement, and getting stuck while starting voice input.
- Fixed guide tour and welcome cards splitting Korean words across lines, non-git project folders showing an error instead of an empty branch menu, and Gemini rate-limit retries being mistaken for a hang.
- Fixed HID devices chosen in the built-in browser failing to connect to the site (#313).
- Fixed the HID device chooser showing stretched flat ovals across the row instead of device names (#314).
- Fixed the Sessions list showing blank rows when returning from another menu or jumping to the top when growing past 40 rows (#315).
- Fixed code search on Linux showing stale results for files reached through symbolic links.
- Fixed the model picker in the agent editor stretching across the entire dialog.

## v1.4.5 - 2026-11-03

This release speeds up ongoing Claude conversations, organizes the Sessions panel by project and branch, and introduces Studio boards, alongside stability improvements for parallel work.

### New features

- **Studio boards** — Group Studio creations into boards from the composer menu, and browse past works with search from the left rail.
- **Projects in Sessions** — Groups sessions by project in the Sessions panel, with sub-categories for each branch when a project has multiple branches.
- **Start screen setting** — Choose what a new desktop window opens with in settings, starting a projectless session by default without accumulating blank tabs (#312).
- **Faster Claude replies** — Ongoing Claude conversations now send only new messages after the initial turn, speeding up replies while falling back when needed.
- **HID devices in the built-in browser** — Websites in the built-in browser can now connect to selected HID hardware (#250).
- **Page actions in Visualize** — Agents can now click, type, and scroll inside open HTML pages in Visualize to inspect interfaces directly.

### Changes

- Changed the Sessions panel to start tasks with a + button in the header and show bots as rows with their status.
- Changed the Request log to show durations in seconds, requested and answering models for substituted requests (#306), and subscription API list prices.
- Changed top-right notifications to alert on app updates, installs, usage-limit pauses, expired sign-ins, and unsaved conversations.
- Changed to-do lists to track pending, in progress, completed, and dropped tasks, preventing blocked steps from turning the progress ring red.
- Adjusted side panels and the Studio gallery to share consistent spacing, empty-state styling, and top and bottom edge fades.

### Bug fixes

- Fixed the app freezing, stuttering, or crashing on memory spikes during heavy operations like code search (#308).
- Fixed an app update install stopping work that was still running (#308).
- Fixed Claude ignoring a message sent after a turn that ended without a reply, as if it were tool output.
- Fixed background worktree checks taking two minutes on Windows after every app launch.
- Fixed plugin updates finishing silently without displaying a completion notice (#307).
- Fixed context popovers being covered on mobile screens (#309) and long timestamps overflowing their column in the Request log (#310).
- Fixed pressing `F2` in the session composer failing to rename the active session.
- Fixed search counts showing full paths instead of relative ones in folders whose names contain numbers and hyphens (#304).

## v1.4.4 - 2026-11-02

Added a Request log in Usage, live sub-agent side panels, session navigation history, and custom provider request options.

### New features

- **Request log** — Added a Request log tab in Usage filtering requests by period, status, and model, showing tokens, cost, duration, and status (#300).
- **Sub-agent side panel** — Added opening sub-agents from the Agents window or composer list; folds with `Ctrl+B` and keeps ended sessions readable.
- **Session navigation** — Added Back and Forward history navigation across sessions and editor locations using `Ctrl/Cmd+[` / `]`, `Alt+Left`/`Right`, and mouse side buttons (#289).
- **Custom provider options** — Added Advanced JSON request parameters, custom HTTP headers, and OpenRouter routing strategies (Auto, Price, Speed, Latency) to model settings (#231).
- **UI zoom shortcuts** — Added zooming the desktop interface between 85% and 150% in 5% increments using `Ctrl/Cmd+=`, `Ctrl/Cmd+-`, and `Ctrl/Cmd+0` (#286).

### Changes

- Adjusted Computer Use to stream element deltas, cache OCR, and send background scrolling and key chords to Mixdog windows without taking foreground focus.
- Changed Mixy to answer what she can settle herself, hand work to another bot only when named or continuing its work, and otherwise use sub-agents.
- Changed handed-off session questions to synchronize between chats, resolving both cards simultaneously when answered, closed, or timed out.
- Changed memory management to automatically save explicit user preferences while requiring confirmation for agent-proposed entries or ambiguous project scopes.
- Changed the desktop bot mascot to appear only when you turn it on in settings.
- Changed the Bots page to hide the Agents group by default; turn it on from the page's ⋯ menu, and your earlier choices are kept.
- Adjusted the to-do list above the composer to read more easily: each item's note now sits on its own line under the item.

### Bug fixes

- Fixed hand-off chains posting multiple completion cards and progress rows by showing one card and one progress row per answer.
- Fixed background runs (memory cycle, web search) showing prompts as session names in the Request log; they now show what they do with an Internal tag.
- Fixed Explore failing to run when configured with an OAuth-only model provider (#301).
- Fixed tasks started outside Git repositories failing when default worktree settings were active (#297).
- Fixed removing a plugin deleting files outside it through links inside the plugin folder, and resolved Windows `EPERM` lock failures during updates (#296).
- Fixed archived bot schedules and webhooks firing while disabled or failing to re-arm upon restoration.
- Fixed silent background terminal commands continuing to appear healthy when stalled past their progress threshold.
- Fixed in-app browser crashing when an iframe was removed during an active command.
- Fixed Computer Use refusing subsequent actions after typing into text fields or failing to release mouse buttons during emergency stops.
- Fixed a session you had just deleted for good coming back when the app closed right after.

## v1.4.3 - 2026-10-31

Added Worktrees settings and branch cleanup, replaced Goal tasks with session todo lists, and introduced customizable composer styles.

### New features

- **Worktrees settings** — Added Settings → Worktrees with disk usage, open and delete actions, and automatic cleanup after 15 worktrees or 30 unused days.
- **Worktree branch actions** — Added New branch, New worktree, and Clean up actions to the branch menu footer, with search highlights; Clean up stays disabled when nothing is safe to remove.
- **Session todo list** — Added a session todo list replacing goal tasks, showing live agent progress, and preserving the last todo and Goal when an agent closes.
- **Composer styles** — Added Simple, Normal, and Detailed composer styles in Settings with live preview, responsive toolbar layouts, and optional question-answer confirmation (#270, #276).
- **Delegation settings** — Added a dedicated Settings → Delegation page for orchestration instructions, and inline prompt editing in Output style with reset to defaults (#291).
- **Sub-agent routine executors** — Added picking an executor sub-agent with its own model for scheduled tasks and webhooks.
- **Claude Desktop Cowork import** — Added importing conversations from Claude Desktop Cowork, listing starred conversations first (#283).
- **Chat path links** — Added opening path links anywhere on your PC from chat: folders open as File panel roots and previewable files open in Visualize (#277).
- **Phone image gestures** — Added pinch, pan, and double-tap zoom for images in chat and Visualize on phones (#275).
- **Fast call usage** — Added a dedicated usage breakdown row for a model's Fast calls, with responsive tables formatted for phone screens (#288).
- **Session lifecycle automation** — Added automatic archival of inactive sessions after 7 days and deletion after 90 days during idle periods.
- **Active PC notification pause** — Added pausing phone push notifications while you are actively using this PC.

### Changes

- Changed tool activity rows to group repetitive operations into counted labels with task names, such as "Worktree management ×4".
- Changed settings and prompt edits made anywhere to apply on the next turn without restarting sessions or breaking prompt caches.
- Changed web search to load immediately without a deferred tool call hop, speeding up lookups.
- Changed remote browser streaming on phones to swipe shut only from the left edge strip, preventing accidental closes during web page interactions.
- Changed the composer bar's agent token usage readout to update within about a second of each model call.
- Adjusted idle garbage collection to sweep external buffer memory, reducing daemon memory footprint.
- Changed a Goal's time limit to an upper bound only; agents finish once work is verified rather than working through the whole period, removing `--time-mode`.

### Bug fixes

- Fixed uncommitted turns being lost after crashes or restarts by adding durable turn handoff and checkpoint recovery.
- Fixed desktop renderer crashing on mouse-up after drag-selecting text.
- Fixed session switching rebuilding transcripts or replaying animations by keeping recent conversations mounted.
- Fixed stalled Goals counting idle time against budget, repeating notifications, and replacing existing Goals without confirmation.
- Fixed connector sign-ins expiring after an hour by requesting refresh tokens, and prevented account switching when reusing removed account names (#285).
- Fixed plugin updates on Windows failing with `EPERM` file-lock errors during folder renames (#284).
- Fixed installation failures caused by onnxruntime-node scripts being removed during embedding prune (#282).
- Fixed memory service startup hanging on orphaned PostgreSQL locks after unexpected process exits (#278).
- Fixed reCAPTCHA and authentication widgets failing in the in-app browser by granting Chrome-compatible storage access.
- Fixed sub-agent reports failing to reach the Lead agent when interrupted by reminders, queued input, or later failures.
- Fixed Computer Use restarting the input host on slow screen reads and reporting observers broken during brief input gaps.
- Fixed recall searches dropping Korean content words in mixed queries, and optimized exact-term scanning.
- Fixed web links and streamed browser tabs on paired phones failing to fit mobile screens or open in Visualize.
- Fixed Settings color rows overlapping descriptions on narrow windows, and prevented instruction edits from overwriting concurrent changes (#287).
- Fixed running `npm ci` inside a worktree emptying the main checkout's `node_modules`; each worktree now installs its own dependencies.
- Fixed resending a task that failed to start (such as in folders without worktree support) repeating "could not be resumed" until restart (#279).
- Fixed Git and Office document tools failing on Windows when a session's temporary folder path grew too long.
- Fixed Vertex AI models Gemini 4 Argon and Gemini 3.8 Flash missing the Reasoning effort control; the choice (Low, Medium, High) now appears and is sent with the request (#292).

## v1.4.2 - 2026-10-29

Improved the agent harness with Explore, a dedicated exploration agent, and stronger verification with the Test Suite skill, plus Vertex AI and several accounts per connector.

### New features

- **Explore** — Added an optional read-only exploration agent the Lead can hand several code questions at once; pick its model under Workflows → Built-in agents.
- **Test Suite skill** — Added a built-in skill for writing, running, diagnosing and pruning a project's tests.
- **Vertex AI** — Added Vertex AI with Gemini, Claude and open models, signing in with a service-account key, your gcloud login or an express-mode API key (#249).
- **Accounts inside a connector** — Added several accounts to one connector; agents use the last-used account unless you name another.
- **Custom provider keys and headers** — Added extra API keys that take over when one runs out of quota, and your own HTTP headers on every request (#233, #239).
- **Connector tool permissions for bots** — Added per-tool Auto, Needs approval and Disabled choices for each connector on a bot's profile (#264).
- **Approve from the on-screen bot** — Added the request and its Allow and Deny buttons to the speech bubble of the on-screen bot.
- **Stop every background command** — Added `/stop` to stop all background commands of a session, plus `/shells` and `/mcp login` on desktop.

### Changes

- Changed agents to fix the cause of a failing check instead of rerunning it, raising its timeout or skipping it.
- Changed bot check-ins and prompt-cache warming to be off by default.
- Changed the desktop and CLI to follow the system proxy, with PAC scripts and exceptions applied per address on desktop, keeping local and LAN hosts direct.
- Changed tool activity rows to show elapsed time only while a command is still running.
- Changed agents stopped as stalled to leave a `stall_abort` row in `history/tool-failures.jsonl`, so a wrongly stopped agent can be reported.
- Changed Git on Windows to start `git.exe` directly and record turn changes with fewer processes, making turns, Undo/Reapply and git tool calls faster.

### Bug fixes

- Fixed stopping commands on Windows: child processes kept running after Stop, Release anyway, a timeout or closing a session, a background command could hang when stopped, and an unrelated older process could be taken for a leftover (#259). Each command now runs in its own Windows job; `MIXDOG_SHELL_ALLOW_BREAKAWAY=1` lets a command start processes outside it.
- Fixed a group room repeating "could not reply" for every bot when the usage limit ran out; it now stops once and says why.
- Fixed session views: long or compacted sessions not scrolling back to their first message, "Session unavailable" while other sessions sent large updates, and the phone's Sessions drawer opening the Bots page instead of the chat.
- Fixed Codex conversations kept only as compressed files failing to import (#262).
- Fixed connector sign-in repeating an "Unrecognized client_id" error after the service forgot Mixdog's registration (#269).
- Fixed the TUI cutting off long sign-in URLs, and added `Ctrl+Y` to copy them (#261).
- Fixed voice input failing to start, and settings or session saves failing, on busy Windows PCs.
- Fixed Chinese and Japanese table cells pushing the table past its frame.
- Fixed Vertex AI models missing the Service tier choice (Standard, Flex, Priority), and queued Flex requests being cut off after a minute (#271).
- Fixed an agent being stopped as stalled after a single failed progress read stopped its activity timer from updating.
- Fixed Computer Use `verify` giving up after 2 seconds regardless of `timeout_ms`, and waiting needlessly when an elevated window's text cannot be read (#274).

## v1.4.1 - 2026-10-27

Fixed sign-in over SSH, PC access setup failures and agents stopping on Anthropic models, and added a view switch for side-by-side Visualize tabs.

### New features

- **Sign-in without a browser** — Added device-code sign-in for ChatGPT and Grok, with the sign-in URL or code shown in the TUI panel over SSH or without a display (#242).
- **Visualize view switch** — Added a view switch to the zoom pill of a side-by-side Visualize tab, to show both panes or one at a time.
- **APK install from chat** — Added opening a downloaded APK in the Android package installer instead of the share sheet (#241).

### Changes

- Changed bots to reach another bot by its bot id when sending to, reading or checking it.
- Changed the sidebar, unread dots and agent spawns to respond faster with long session lists.

### Bug fixes

- Fixed PC access setup failing on PCs whose drive root carries an inherit-only permission, and showing why an approval did not finish (#251).
- Fixed agents on Anthropic models being stopped as stale while thinking or writing a large file (#248).
- Fixed agents on custom Responses routes going stale before their first output (#244).
- Fixed Computer Use, Browser Use and sign-in callbacks failing with a "bad port" error on some PCs.
- Fixed choosing a main model on a fallback's provider failing with "duplicate route provider".
- Fixed an automatic switch to a fallback model sending every MCP tool at once.
- Fixed imported Claude and Codex conversations losing early history, titles or pages, and showed their tool use as collapsed activity rows (#245).
- Fixed orphaned worktrees staying behind and the default branch being taken into a managed worktree (#247).
- Fixed a bot showing as working after its delegated work ended, and a compacted session missing its done dot.
- Fixed the prompt cache being rebuilt after an interrupted request or a restart.
- Fixed a table or code block that ends a reply losing its bottom border, and narrow phone tables losing their cell gap.

## v1.4.0 - 2026-10-27

Improved remote work from your phone together with Browser Use and Computer Use, and streamlined the agent harness to skip redundant checks and finish work faster.

### New features

- **Remote PC screen** — Added viewing and controlling your PC screen from your phone over a direct WebRTC connection with special keys and an on-PC status pill.
- **PC access** — Added optional access to administrator prompts, the lock screen and `Ctrl`+`Alt`+`Del` from your phone, approved once in Computer Use setup or with your Windows password.
- **Browser live view** — Added streaming the in-app browser to your phone over WebRTC, fitting takeover pages to your screen with direct typing from your mobile keyboard.
- **Notification controls** — Added per-device notification settings, conversation mutes, quiet hours and error notifications under Settings → Notifications, with Allow on approval notifications (#221, thanks @dislight1123).
- **Bot-delegated work** — Added one live line per job under the reply for work a bot delegates, showing progress and letting you answer questions in chat.
- **Saved sign-ins** — Added automatic sign-in with saved logins and one-time codes, managed under Settings → Authentication, without the model ever seeing the secrets.
- **Chrome login import** — Added importing Chrome saved logins, including newer app-bound encrypted ones, into the rebuilt Logins page with a saved/stay-signed-in switch.
- **Sign-in from your mail** — Added opening sign-in links and filling codes from your verified mail, and remembering which identity provider each site used.
- **Saved login in Chrome and Edge** — Added Computer Use filling a saved login into your own Chrome or Edge without exposing it to the model.
- **Prompt-cache warming** — Added automatic prompt-cache warming for Anthropic models under Settings → Context, learning your return habits and warming bots ahead of scheduled runs.
- **More Google connections** — Added connecting more Google accounts to Gmail, Calendar and Drive, choosing the account per request, with a clear sign-in prompt.

### Changes

- Changed agents to verify once after all edits instead of mid-task, run independent tool calls together, and keep progress updates short.
- Changed Settings into four sections: Basics, AI behavior, Integrations and Support.
- Changed the Sessions menu to let you choose which sidebar sections to show.
- Changed typing, session and tab switching, Search, Settings, side panels, the terminal and Changes to open instantly, with smoother status animations.
- Changed approvals from bot-delegated sessions to appear in every chat waiting on them, with the same wording and keys on every approval card.
- Changed session and bot rows to show an amber triangle for an approval wait, a question icon for a question, and waiting work counts.
- Changed bot task sessions and sub-agents to carry their own unread dot, read together with the chat they report to.
- Changed a paired phone to read, preview, download and open files the same way the PC does.
- Changed the `@` file picker to rank shallow paths first, open with recent work, and find files in linked folders (#228, thanks @reeves-ai-lch).
- Changed Visualize to open pages from any local folder, naming index pages by their folder.
- Changed the usage popup and pinned usage rail to show each limit as one line over a full-width bar.
- Changed the shell tool to accept an optional working directory and refuse sleeps of 2 seconds or more.
- Changed agent terminal runs and browser pages to reveal their tab on the PC and paired devices, opened directly from transcript lines.
- Changed Browser Use to cap background pages per session and close them after a turn finishes.
- Changed retry waits to show a fixed reason and a live countdown instead of raw error text.
- Changed bot chats to show no changed-files card under a reply, separate distant messages, and share one line for hand-off and time.
- Changed the language list to show Korean by its own name.
- Changed Mixy's regular check-in to run every hour by default, with the interval selectable under Settings → Bots.
- Changed the phone app to connect to your PC directly when the network allows, falling back to the relay automatically.
- Changed side panels to share one width, adjustable from 280 to 1160 pixels.
- Adjusted the phone side dock to close by swiping anywhere on the sheet, and animated drawer rows and text shimmers more smoothly.

### Bug fixes

- Fixed the split-pane layout being lost when the app's local storage is reset.
- Fixed panel edges, dividers and colours shifting when a side panel opens or closes.
- Fixed the phone drawer's content disappearing while it slides closed.
- Fixed the pinned bot leaving the composer's right end after a side panel closed, and chats dropping by a line on entry.
- Fixed a bot's row not spinning or taking unread dots while its task sessions work.
- Fixed clicking a desktop notification leaving the sidebar on the previous session, or doing nothing with the window hidden.
- Fixed answering a question card at the end of a chat stopping the transcript from following the reply.
- Fixed task sessions created with an explicit model failing with "service is not defined".
- Fixed Mixy's regular check-in running while you were still using the desktop app.
- Fixed Computer Use typing into windows that raise themselves, and writing into read-only or disabled fields.
- Fixed saved passwords longer than 4,096 characters being cut short, and secrets shorter than four characters going unmasked in chats.
- Fixed a queued retry of a failed turn, and a routine's skill choice, being lost after a restart (#229, thanks @22nsuk).
- Fixed quota auto-resume over SSH reading the server's quota instead of the PC's when the PC holds the sign-in (#232, thanks @22nsuk).
- Fixed `Option`+`Left`/`Right` not moving by word in text fields on macOS (#230, thanks @wudys).
- Fixed an agent profile's context selection not being preserved (#226, thanks @22nsuk), and Cursor failing on stored context conflicts (#225, thanks @22nsuk).
- Fixed a waiting task session reading as stalled, and a disabled connector account that could not be turned back on.
- Fixed a sign-in-expired turn error losing its retry, and the browser panel showing a blank page after its last page closed.
- Fixed clicking an attachment in a long or compacted conversation failing with "This conversation has no such attachment."
- Fixed the phone agent panel showing a duplicate Profile title above its own tabs.
- Fixed the side panel's Changes view being titled Profile after a bot's profile was last open there.
- Fixed the session list and chat on Android phones freezing after a fling and then jumping.
- Fixed sidebar section headers remaining highlighted after a click, and their spinner hiding while the menu button showed.
- Fixed compacting a conversation dropping current skills and rules instead of rebuilding them from active sources.
- Fixed Mixy appearing on her own after a failed startup check, reading out check-ins and then vanishing (#243, thanks @Jichiro-S).
- Fixed existing sessions ignoring current compaction settings, and forks compacting too early (#237, thanks @22nsuk; #238, thanks @skywhale345).
- Fixed bots asking you in chat to solve a CAPTCHA or sign-in step instead of handing you the page.

## v1.3.5 - 2026-10-24

Added emoji reactions, regular check-ins and SSH server model logins, with verified Google connectors, phone drawer swipes and broad fixes.

### New features

- **Emoji reactions** — Added bot emoji reactions on user messages with a toggle in Settings → General → "Reactions".
- **Regular check-ins** — Added 30-minute background reviews under Settings → Profile where your representative bot checks active sessions and wakes only when something needs attention.
- **SSH server logins** — Added running models using an SSH server's own provider logins and setting a private key file when connecting (#204).
- **Google connectors** — Added built-in Google Calendar and Drive connectors with verified sign-in, requiring all permissions and keeping Gmail on app passwords.
- **Phone swipe navigation** — Added horizontal swiping anywhere on the phone to open the session list or files dock.

### Changes

- Changed Office previews to render through Microsoft Office when LibreOffice is missing, detect installs immediately, and ask for the password of protected files.
- Changed schedules, bots, rooms and Lead sessions to be renamable from their menus, keeping one-shot run times intact.
- Changed Linux secret storage to fall back to protected local files when no keychain is available, explaining why keys cannot be read (#204).
- Changed bot chats to show exchanges with other sessions inline, and clicking the representative bot's speech bubble dismisses it.
- Changed the app to open faster by showing your chat and session list before agents load, and switching back to a recent session now shows it instantly.

### Bug fixes

- Fixed switched-off room bots continuing to take turns, naming them clearly when addressed (#215).
- Fixed approval cards stealing focus while typing in the composer, and showed a waiting browser-approval mark in the phone session list.
- Fixed long tool outputs on the phone failing to load through Show full output, and opened chats sticking on loading skeletons.
- Fixed switching between sessions sending an in-progress composer draft to the wrong chat (#217).
- Fixed right-click and row menus closing unexpectedly whenever a background agent updated or transcript scrolled.
- Fixed browser auto-sign-in failing on CAPTCHA challenges or worker crashes, keeping consistent browser identity across Cloudflare checks.
- Fixed broken emoji surrogate pairs failing model requests, and isolated full quota windows so they block only affected models (#209).
- Fixed finished agents being marked as canceled when closed, and allowed editing definitions directly in place (#211, #216).

## v1.3.4 - 2026-10-23

Fixed phone scrolling that stopped or jumped, model lists missing provider models, and tables shaking while a reply streams.

### Bug fixes

- Fixed a fast flick on Android stopping partway in the session list, also right after returning to the app.
- Fixed scrolling up through a chat on Android stuttering or jumping partway.
- Fixed tables shaking sideways while a reply streams in a coding chat.
- Fixed a room's Stop missing a member reply, approval or message that finished just after it (#201).
- Fixed options picked on a question card being lost when answering from the composer (#202).
- Fixed a sub-agent failing to start when its model was given by its display name (#203).
- Fixed agents asking you to close their finished sub-agents instead of closing them themselves.
- Fixed model lists in the agent editor, bot profile and composer missing models from OpenCode Go, OpenRouter and other providers (#205).

## v1.3.3 - 2026-10-22

Added a 12/24-hour time setting, legacy Office attachments and long-paste folding, with smoother phone scrolling, steadier compaction and broad room and bot fixes.

### New features

- **Time format** — Added Settings → General → "Time format" (phone: Settings → Display) to show times as System, 12-hour or 24-hour.
- **Legacy Office attachments** — Added sending `.xls`, `.doc` and `.ppt` files; they are converted through LibreOffice when the Office feature is installed (#163).
- **Long pastes** — Added folding pastes over 1,000 characters in the composer, and sent messages longer than 20 lines behind "Show more" (#186).
- **Everyone in a room** — Added `@all` to address every room member, and naming a room member from another session to reach it (#164, #180).
- **New task without a project** — Added `Ctrl+Alt+N` to open a new task that is not tied to a project (#185).
- **All usage accounts** — Added expanding every signed-in account in the usage panel and the side rail.
- **Image input per model** — Added an Auto/On/Off "Image input" choice to each custom provider model (#191).
- **Goal bar** — Added a progress ring, a compact count-only bar and an inline stop confirmation to the Goal bar.

### Changes

- Changed the session list to hide sub-agent and archived sessions; idle sub-agent sessions are archived after 3 days and deleted after 30 (#165).
- Changed a bot's model change to apply to its open chats from the next turn (#166).
- Changed bot approvals to ask only in the bot's own chats, with room members following their home chat's rules (#167).
- Changed Mixy's look to both ears down and a thick tail with a lighter tip.
- Changed the representative bot's position to one dropdown in Settings, added a Free placement, and showed its uploaded picture (#178, #179).
- Changed agent sessions in the sidebar to show only the model name, and a bot's task session to show as one result card.
- Changed coding replies to appear word by word, with finished tool groups named in the past tense and the status line last.
- Changed custom providers to show their registered name in model pickers, usage, workflows and notices.
- Changed connectors with several accounts, such as three Gmail accounts, to show as one row and one icon.
- Changed tapping a notification to open the session at its latest message.
- Changed phone browser tabs to pair directly instead of showing the Add to Home Screen guide.
- Changed the Android notification icon to the Mixdog mark.

### Bug fixes

- Fixed scrolling up on the phone stopping midway or jumping when older messages loaded.
- Fixed taps and drags not reaching the browser panel when using Mixdog remotely from an iPhone or iPad.
- Fixed agent reports, tool results and late MCP tools being lost after a conversation was compacted.
- Fixed the conversation stopping to follow a long reply, or releasing it when text was pressed.
- Fixed the unread dot staying on a chat you were reading in a side pane.
- Fixed editing a previous message dropping its attachments, and rewinds that ignored later history (#186).
- Fixed open conversations not noticing agents that were enabled or disabled (#184).
- Fixed replies stopping at the output limit and a broken reasoning-effort judge staying broken (#183).
- Fixed a removed bot continuing its work in rooms and conversations (#180).

## v1.2.0 - 2026-10-13

This release introduces the Changes panel and per-turn change cards with per-turn undo and reapply controls, keeps earlier conversation history visible after compaction, and adds a built-in visualization tool for interactive UI mockups and diagrams. Remote workflows expand with SSH server connections, isolated Git worktree sessions, background shell management, and direct file downloads on paired phones. The interface also brings higher contrast styling, smoother mobile scrolling, and flexible session organization.

### New features

- After a conversation is compacted, its earlier messages, tool cards, and diffs stay readable above a "Conversation compacted" divider instead of disappearing. They are kept for display only (never sent to the model), reload by scrolling up after a restart, use up to about 32 MB per session (with the oldest trimmed first), filter sensitive values like other history, and are deleted with the session, while continued sessions link back instead of duplicating them. Undo, reapply, and retry are not offered for turns before the compaction.
- The Changes panel provides a single scrolling view of every changed file's diff with tabs at the side: the "Changes" tab shows all files, while clicking a file in a turn card opens just that file's tab. The panel works without Git using the session's own change records, highlights syntax, wraps long lines instead of scrolling horizontally, folds or unfolds when clicking anywhere on a file row, opens a file in a tab with `↗`, undoes a file with `↶`, and lists files outside the project read-only with their full path in the tooltip. Closing the last tab closes the panel.
- A turn changes card under each turn displays the number of changed files, a +N −N line diff summary, a View changes button, and the list of modified files.
- Redesigned tool cards show the change made by each individual edit rather than the turn's running total, rendered in the same diff view as the Changes panel, and display line additions and deletions while the tool is still running.
- A built-in visualize tool generates project mockups and inline diagrams (Mermaid, SVG, ECharts, HTML, and Markdown) in dedicated side-panel tabs. You can inspect elements, capture page errors, leave pinned feedback with data selections for the next message, compare and restore versions, and export designs to PNG or PDF.
- Git worktree sessions let you work on isolated branches without touching your current checkout. A branch chip above the composer lets you choose or create a new worktree branch when starting a task, with guarded merges that prevent merge conflict residue.
- Connect to remote servers over SSH from Settings > Connection. Mixdog installs automatically on the server, opens in its own window with a Ports panel with port forwarding, remote file browsing, and terminals, and proxies model calls through your PC so credentials never need to live on the server.
- Paired phones can now download and share assistant-produced files and generated media directly from chat links, complete with transfer progress, retries, and cancellation (saves to Downloads on Android and the share sheet on iOS; with the next Android app update or iOS app build) (#40). Paired phones are also strictly limited to registered projects and files produced in that session.
- Background shell commands can be stopped directly from the app or remotely. Finished commands stay listed until dismissed instead of disappearing immediately, and the composer island's jobs panel expands inline to show running background commands alongside agents with cumulative token usage and tool call counts.
- Move a session to another project from the sidebar menu or by drag and drop without moving its folder on disk; sessions located in a project's subfolders and worktrees are grouped under that project automatically.
- Side panels on phones (browser, terminal, changes, and preview) share the same header as on PC, complete with tabs, a menu to switch panels, and a close button. In the phone browser, `+` opens a new tab in that session's side panel, and tabs switch and close just like on the PC (needs the updated PC app).
- Images you send retain thumbnails after restarting the app, and visualize and HTML file cards display a real visual preview of the page rendered locally in an isolated sandbox with no network access for files inside the project.
- The composer island lists running agents in the same format as the Agents window, and automatically hides the shell section when no background shells are active.
- Closing the last terminal, browser, or file tab closes the side panel, and opening the terminal again starts a fresh tab (based on #49 by @moveju112).

  Korean text breaks where a reader expects, a geometry check refuses slides
  whose declared alignments the browser cannot confirm, and `render` shows
  each HTML page beside its PowerPoint render. The script route stays for
  decks that want the kit's measured devices, or when no local browser exists.

- Inserting or deleting rows and columns in a workbook without Excel now
  rewrites everything that names those cells, the way Excel does: formulas on
  every sheet, defined names and print areas, conditional formats,
  validations, chart series, pivot sources, filters, links, merges, tables and
  drawings. The cells used to move while their references stayed put, so a
  report total kept summing the old range and read 72,200 where Excel read
  74,700. An edit whose references cannot be rewritten is refused, with the
  list, before anything changes.

- PDFs and composed spreadsheet bands keep Korean dates, times, fractions and
  amounts on one line. "10월 14일", "14시 30분", "3분의 1", "12만 6천 원" and
  "24억 원" no longer break in the middle, which had split a decision date or
  a saving across two lines.

- Office files come out the same whether Microsoft Office or the built-in
  portable writer produced them. A long side-by-side comparison of both
  aligned Word spacing, compatibility mode and tables; Excel autofit, indents,
  borders, print setup and preset charts; PowerPoint Korean wrapping, East
  Asian fonts, footers, cover crops, shadows and transparency; and PDF
  alignment and table widths. Review checks report the same issues on both
  backends, Excel charts can read another sheet's range, and `set_chart_data`
  keeps a chart's links and series names.

- Computer Use runs on macOS and Linux. Desktop builds for those systems
  bundle a native backend that speaks the Windows host's protocol and enforces
  the same action lists and limits. A sequence can now also act on several
  elements of one observation: each later step re-proves its element against
  the live accessibility tree, and the chain stops at a window switch, a
  failure, or a disabled or off-screen element.

- The phone app opens and reconnects faster and moves far less data. The
  transcript shows right after the first sync, short reconnects resume as
  deltas instead of a full resync, the phone mirrors only the tab it shows,
  the collapsed turn review reads file names and counts without patch text,
  and slow project searches no longer hold up other calls. A phone app kept
  open checks for a new deploy when it comes back to the foreground, and
  adopts one off screen even mid-turn.

- The daemon uses less memory and stalls less: sessions save only what
  changed, the usage ledger works off the main thread, file locks and git
  calls no longer block it, and long transcripts page in 1 MB steps. Desktop
  and phone render streaming Markdown and touch scrolling with fewer layouts,
  and the web app's transcript no longer jitters while rows are measured.

- Voice input shows that it is preparing until capture really starts, warms
  up transcription while you speak, and transcribes faster without blocking
  the app.

- Tool results cost the model fewer tokens. `read` returns its rows without
  line numbers — the TUI and desktop still draw the gutter — for about 16%
  fewer tokens on recorded sessions; shell and task notices are shorter; and
  edits report paths relative to the working directory.

- Compaction carries less stale material in large context windows. The
  verbatim conversation and the recent tool history kept through a Compact are
  capped at 20,000 tokens instead of growing with the window. A browser
  snapshot or desktop observation that a later one of the same page or window
  replaced keeps only its outcome and a pointer to the archived original, and
  older replies drop their opaque provider replay while keeping their tool
  calls and results.

- A provider that is briefly unavailable no longer ends the turn the moment
  its own retries run out. While nothing has reached the screen, the turn
  waits through a few more recovery cycles, from 15 seconds up to a minute,
  and follows a server's own Retry-After. When a stream is cut while a tool
  call's arguments are still arriving, that call is not run, and the model is
  told to split the content across smaller calls instead of resending it
  whole.

- Cursor and Antigravity (Gemini) OAuth are separate switches under Settings →
  Developer, and each turns on only after you confirm the risk of account
  restrictions that comes with using that provider through OAuth. The
  `MIXDOG_DEV_PROVIDERS` environment variable no longer turns them on.

- The conversation no longer jumps when the bars above the composer open or
  close: they slide over the motion instead of shifting the transcript by
  their full height at once, and opening a session no longer flashes a turn
  review count that disappears a moment later.

- Renaming a file or folder in the explorer keeps its open editor tabs on the
  new path. A file with unsaved edits is refused until it is saved, since its
  buffer belongs to the old path.

- Studio cleans up in bulk: the selected items, everything before a date,
  entries whose files are gone, or all of one kind. Settings → About lists a

- An automatic goal turn that calls no tool now waits instead of prompting
  again.

## v0.9.173 - 2026-09-22

- A restored queued message keeps the text the daemon confirmed. Restoring one
  publishes twice in the same breath — the local guess first, the daemon's
  answer a moment later — and both were stamped with the clock. When they
  landed in the same millisecond the prompt treated the second as the first and
  kept the guess, so an edited message could come back subtly wrong. The prompt
  now follows the text itself, not only the stamp.

- Jumping twice in one instant no longer loses the second jump. Two "go to this
  line" requests inside the same millisecond carried the same stamp, and the
  editor read only the stamp, so the second one was dropped and the cursor sat
  on the first line.

- A search that crashes no longer takes the whole search engine with it. The
  engine already knew how to answer one bad request with an error and keep
  serving, but the shipped build was compiled so that any crash killed the
  process instead — losing every other search in flight and the warm file
  index. It now survives, answers that one request with an error, and keeps
  its caches. If a crash does happen while files are being collected, the
  collected paths are still published rather than quietly disappearing from
  the answer.

- Apply and Delete on a local provider row sit on the same line. They differed
  by two pixels because the row mixed a taller input with a shorter button.

- Cleaning up code tells you when a tool is not the tool you think it is. If a
  formatter or linter with the same name is reachable on your machine but is
  not the one Mixdog runs, the report now names both, with versions — running
  that other binary says nothing about the result you were shown. A cleanup run
  also separates findings in files you have already touched from findings in
  files that are untouched in the repository, so applying fixes to a whole
  directory no longer rewrites files you never meant to change.

- Updating your installed app no longer stops because your antivirus removed a
  file the update discards anyway. Staging unpacked the whole installed app and
  deleted the part it was about to replace; one quarantined renderer asset was
  enough to abort the deploy.

## v0.9.172 - 2026-09-21

- A page no longer opens by announcing downloads it never made. Saved files
  belong to the session, but each page tracked what it had reported starting
  from zero, so every page opened afterwards greeted the caller with the whole
  backlog — a search page reporting a file another tab had saved minutes
  earlier. A new page starts already aware of what happened before it existed;
  a file saved while it is open still reaches it.

- The browser's own faults no longer read as the page's. A timed-out CDP call,
  a child frame that could not be attached, an interception that could not be
  answered — all of them were logged as page console errors, so a reply about a
  healthy site could open with `CDP Runtime.evaluate timed out` as if the site
  had logged it. They stay readable through `console`, marked `[browser]`, and
  no longer count among the errors a page is answerable for.

- A deadline reached behind an open dialog says so. An alert, confirm or prompt
  freezes the page's main thread, so the next call died on its timeout with
  nothing but the deadline — and the obvious retry timed out the same way. The
  error now names the dialog and its text, and says to answer it with
  `handle_dialog` before acting on the page again.

- A client-side route change is answered with the screen it produced, not the
  one the caller left. Single-page apps move the address with `history.pushState`
  and render the new view a moment later; no document loads, so the settle saw a
  quiet page and returned at once — and an `expect.url` was satisfied by the new
  address before anything was drawn. Clicking "Learn" on react.dev answered with
  the home page under the `/learn` address. When an action changes the address
  without a load, the reply now waits for the page to go quiet and a URL
  condition may not cut that short. Measured on the real-device harness:
  navigate, click and snapshot latencies are unchanged, because only same-
  document route changes take the extra wait.

- A WebSocket detail shows the upgrade request it actually sent. Only the
  address and the handshake response were recorded, so `network` answered with
  an empty request-header section — and a refused upgrade is usually explained
  by `Origin`, `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` or a cookie. Credentials stay redacted.

- A click that opens a tab is no longer reported as a click that did nothing.
  A `target="_blank"` link leaves the current document untouched, so the reply
  answered "No observable change" and told the caller to look for a covering
  element — while the page it had just opened sat in `list_tabs` unmentioned.
  The reply now names the page that opened and how to act on it.

- `drag` takes snapshot-free targets like every other pointer action. Its two
  ends only accepted refs or raw coordinates, and the elements a page makes
  draggable — cards, list rows, drop zones — often carry no accessible name and
  therefore no ref, so moving one meant grounding a visual snapshot first even
  when the CSS selector was known. `target` and `dropTarget` now name the two
  ends, resolved together in one observation; refs and coordinates work as
  before, and both ends still have to be addressed the same way.

- A saved file is no longer announced as a failed request. An address that
  turns into a download cancels its own navigation, and Chromium reports that
  cancellation as `net::ERR_ABORTED`, so a reply that listed the download also
  listed it as a recent network failure. Cancelled requests — downloads, fetches
  the page abandoned, navigations replaced by another — stay readable through
  `network` but are no longer volunteered as faults of the page; a request that
  genuinely failed still is.

- A `brief` reply no longer turns one filled field into a page-wide change. It
  compares against the caller's previous observation, and when that observation
  was capped or filtered it had never reported the rest of the page — so every
  element outside it was listed as "changed or new". Filling three boxes on a
  form answered with fifteen elements, and typing one search word answered with
  a hundred and forty-six. The reply now keeps what the action demonstrably
  changed apart from what the earlier observation simply never covered, and says
  how much of the page that observation held. Nothing is omitted either way.

- Request headers in `network` are the ones that were actually sent. Chromium
  reports a provisional set first and adds language, encoding, client hints and
  cookies afterwards, so a request detail could show two headers and read as if
  the page never asked for Korean content. The later set is merged in;
  credentials are still named and never shown. Header names are case-insensitive
  and the two reports spell them differently, so the merge keeps one entry per
  header — the spelling and value that went on the wire — instead of listing
  `User-Agent` and `user-agent` as if the request carried both.

- Sites see Browser Use as the Chrome build that renders them. The agent string
  still carried the desktop app version and the Electron runtime, while the
  client hints the same pages received named Chromium alone; GitHub answered
  that contradiction with a sign-in wall on a public repository. The browser
  partition now presents the plain Chrome string — one less fingerprint, and
  fewer "unsupported browser" detours — and an emulated user agent still wins
  when a task asks for one.

- Pages that keep attaching frames can be observed again. Portals and news
  front pages open ad slots and widgets in bursts, and a snapshot that started
  mid-burst used to give up with "frame topology changed during observation" —
  reproducibly, on the first and second try. Observations have no side effects,
  so the collector now waits briefly for the burst to settle and reads again,
  up to a small ceiling, instead of handing the caller an error for a page that
  was merely busy. When a reading still fails, the reply now says the page is
  loaded and only the reading of it failed, so the next step is to observe
  again rather than abandon a page that is fine.

- A page reports only its own failures. Requests and console errors from the
  previous document stayed in the ledgers, so a snapshot of a healthy page could
  list aborted requests from the site visited before it, and `console` on a
  clean page could answer with the errors of the page before — both sending the
  reader after a fault that was not there. Loading a new document clears them;
  navigating inside the same document keeps them, because nothing reloaded.

- Browser Use display races are no longer failures. A capture that loses to a
  navigation or a window resize now answers with a resample marker instead of
  an error, because the pane was always going to ask again for whatever the
  page shows next. Ordinary browsing used to fill the app log with capture
  failures — seventeen in one harness run, none now — and a paired phone
  reported the same race as "could not connect to browser screen"; it now
  re-samples at the active cadence and reports only a display that genuinely
  stops making progress.

- Clear Browser Use browsing data. The browser pane has an eraser button that
  removes the cache, the data sites stored on this device, and cookies, each
  as its own decision: cache is preselected because losing it costs one slower
  reload, while cookies sign you out of every site and are never the default.
  Each scope is cleared on its own, so one failure is reported as a failure
  instead of disappearing behind the scopes that worked. Clearing cookies also
  rewrites the sealed file that carries session sign-ins across restarts, so a
  login you cleared does not come back the next time the app opens — and if
  that file cannot be rewritten, cookies are reported as not cleared rather
  than as done. Until now the shared partition grew on disk with no way to
  reclaim it.

- Browser Use `performance` metrics report the memory of the process painting
  the page, not just the JavaScript heap: a page whose images and layers hold
  the memory used to look small. The reading names the process, since one
  renderer can paint several pages of the same site.

- Browser Use domain policy covers peer connections. When an operator
  restricts the domains a page may reach, WebRTC no longer walks past the
  filter through STUN and TURN: peer connections are refused in the page and
  in every child frame. Without a domain policy nothing changes, and this
  remains containment for page code rather than a network boundary.

- Browser Use element screenshots. `snapshot mode=visual` accepts `ref` or
  `target` and returns that element as its own image. The box is measured in
  top-document CSS pixels — same-process frames fold their offset in on the
  page side, a cross-origin frame adds its session offset without the hit
  test that guards input, because a picture dispatches nothing and a frame
  under a CSS transform still deserves one — and the crop is scaled by the
  image-to-viewport ratio, so it holds
  on a zoomed or high-DPI display. An element taller or wider than the window
  is cut out of the document capture instead of the viewport, so a long table
  or article arrives whole rather than ending at the fold; only a page too
  large to capture falls back to the visible part, and says so. The image is
  inspection-only: it is never bound as coordinate grounding, because the ref
  remains the way to act on the element. `mode=semantic`, `fullPage` and
  `format=pdf` refuse a target rather than ignoring it.

- Browser Use input fidelity. `drag` now completes a page's own HTML5 drag:
  Chromium's drag interception hands over the payload the page started and
  the gesture finishes as `dragEnter`/`dragOver`/`drop`, which is what a
  kanban card, a sortable list or a file drop zone actually listens for;
  pages that only track mouse events keep the previous path. `type` sends a
  real key event per character instead of inserting the whole string, so
  keystroke-driven autocomplete and combo boxes react, while characters
  outside the US layout (Korean, emoji) are still inserted as text. `press`
  sends the US key codes for punctuation (`.` was Delete, `-` was Insert),
  keeps a shortcut from typing a character, and no longer infers Shift from a
  capital letter, which had turned `Control+A` into `Control+Shift+A`.
  `upload` drops files on an element that never opens a file chooser, with a
  guard that neutralizes an unhandled drop — otherwise the browser navigates
  the page to the dropped file — and reports plainly when nothing accepted it.

- Browser Use observation fidelity. `scroll text=` searches frames and shadow
  roots like `read` and `expect` do, picks one match across them, and no
  longer scrolls to a collapsed element. `expect.text` normalizes spaces
  within a line but keeps line breaks, so indented markup matches while two
  separate blocks never merge into one sentence. Console diagnostics keep
  what a page logged: object arguments arrive as a readable preview instead
  of an empty message, entries name the script and the line a reader would
  open, and an uncaught bare `throw` carries its location. Snapshots mark
  `aria-hidden`, a failed native `select` lists the options it did find, and
  `aria-labelledby` resolves inside a shadow root.

- Browser Use counts the diagnostics it could not fit. A page report shows the
  three newest console errors and network failures, which read as the whole
  story: twelve failures arrived as three. The report now names the total and
  points at `console` or `network` whenever the list is capped.

- Browser Use admits when a page excerpt stops early. The visible text in a
  snapshot is capped, and the report said only "condensed", so a long article
  read as if the excerpt were the whole page. Both snapshot paths — the
  accessibility capture and the DOM fallback — now mark a clipped excerpt, and
  the report names how much it carries and says the page holds more.

- Attachments report the size of the image they actually produced. Fitting an
  image to a vision patch budget trims the edges one at a time, which can ask
  for a box the picture does not fill; the rendition then came out smaller
  than the size reported beside it, and coordinates mapped through that size
  were off. The resize now reports the dimensions of the produced image.

- Browser Use says where a page script failed. `evaluate` kept only the first
  line of the browser's error, so a script of several lines reported
  `TypeError: ...` with nothing to locate it. The failure now carries the
  innermost stack frame with it, and the integration harness pins the position
  a throw on a later line reports.

- Browser Use names a PDF instead of reporting an empty page. Opening a link
  to a PDF committed the address, but the guest has no viewer for it, so the
  snapshot showed an untitled page with no text and console noise about a
  blocked viewer stylesheet — nothing that says what happened. The page report
  now states that the document is a PDF this browser cannot display and that
  the file has to be read from its URL, and the failures Chromium's own
  bundled components raise for their `chrome-extension://` resources no longer
  appear as the page's console or network errors. The integration harness
  covers the navigation, the quiet report, and a later snapshot of the page.

- Browser Use stops bouncing `close_tab` off the visible tab. `list_tabs`
  prints the visible page with an ordinary page id, so aiming `close_tab` at
  it was answered with `unknown background tab "p12"; call list_tabs` — the
  listing that handed the id out. The refusal now says the page belongs to
  the browser panel and points at navigating it elsewhere or `hide`, and
  unrelated names still report an unknown background tab.

- Browser Use says what a leave confirmation actually did. A page that guards
  unsaved work stopped a navigation with a `beforeunload` dialog, and the
  reply asked for `handle_dialog` — but Chromium answers that confirmation
  itself, so the call always came back "no JavaScript dialog is currently
  open" while repeating the navigation repeated the same instruction. The
  reply now states that the navigation was abandoned and the page stayed,
  that there is nothing left to answer, and that the work the page holds has
  to be finished or discarded first; the integration harness holds the whole
  sequence, including the navigation going through once the guard is gone.

- Browser Use locale emulation reaches the server. `emulate locale` set
  `navigator.language` alone, so the page kept asking for the old language
  and sites negotiated content the emulation contradicted; it now carries the
  locale as `Accept-Language` too, and clearing it restores the browser's own
  negotiation.

## v0.9.171 - 2026-09-18

- Release recovery: the staged production relay artifact is keyed to the run
  alone (`production-relay-<run_id>`) and uploads with `overwrite: true`. The
  name carried the run attempt, but a partial re-run preserves the successful
  `stage-production-web-relay` job while re-running
  `deploy-production-web-relay` as a dependent of the failed job, so the
  attempt-scoped artifact never existed and the deploy died on "Artifact not
  found" before it could reach production. That is exactly how v0.9.170
  published its GitHub release and npm package without deploying the web
  relay. `overwrite: true` keeps a full re-run, where the stage job does
  execute again, from colliding with the earlier attempt's artifact, and the
  release gate asserts both the name and the overwrite.

# Contributor Covenant Code of Conduct

## Our Pledge

We as members, contributors, and leaders pledge to make participation in our community a harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of age, body size, visible or invisible disability, ethnicity, sex characteristics, gender identity and expression, level of experience, education, socio-economic status, nationality, personal appearance, race, caste, color, religion, or sexual identity and orientation.

We pledge to act and interact in ways that contribute to an open, welcoming, diverse, inclusive, and healthy community.

## Our Standards

Examples of behavior that contributes to a positive environment for our community include:

* Demonstrating empathy and kindness toward other people
* Being respectful of differing opinions, viewpoints, and experiences
* Giving and gracefully accepting constructive feedback
* Accepting responsibility and apologizing to those affected by our mistakes, and learning from the experience
* Focusing on what is best not just for us as individuals, but for the overall community

Examples of unacceptable behavior include:

* The use of sexualized language or imagery, and sexual attention or advances of any kind
* Trolling, insulting or derogatory comments, and personal or political attacks
* Public or private harassment
* Publishing others' private information, such as a physical or email address, without their explicit permission
* Other conduct which could reasonably be considered inappropriate in a professional setting

## Enforcement Responsibilities

Community leaders are responsible for clarifying and enforcing our standards of acceptable behavior and will take appropriate and fair corrective action in response to any behavior that they deem inappropriate, threatening, offensive, or harmful.

Community leaders have the right and responsibility to remove, edit, or reject comments, commits, code, wiki edits, issues, and other contributions that are not aligned to this Code of Conduct, and will communicate reasons for moderation decisions when appropriate.

## Scope

This Code of Conduct applies within all community spaces, and also applies when an individual is officially representing the community in public spaces. Examples of representing our community include using an official e-mail address, posting via an official social media account, or acting as an appointed representative at an online or offline event.

## Enforcement

Instances of abusive, harassing, or otherwise unacceptable behavior may be reported to the community leaders responsible for enforcement at support@mixdog.ai. All complaints will be reviewed and investigated promptly and fairly.

All community leaders are obligated to respect the privacy and security of the reporter of any incident.

## Enforcement Guidelines

Community leaders will follow these Community Impact Guidelines in determining the consequences for any action they deem in violation of this Code of Conduct:

### 1. Correction

**Community Impact**: Use of inappropriate language or other behavior deemed unprofessional or unwelcome in the community.

**Consequence**: A private, written warning from community leaders, providing clarity around the nature of the violation and an explanation of why the behavior was inappropriate. A public apology may be requested.

### 2. Warning

**Community Impact**: A violation through a single incident or series of actions.

**Consequence**: A warning with consequences for continued behavior. No interaction with the people involved, including unsolicited interaction with those enforcing the Code of Conduct, for a specified period of time. This includes avoiding interactions in community spaces as well as external channels like social media. Violating these terms may lead to a temporary or permanent ban.

### 3. Temporary Ban

**Community Impact**: A serious violation of community standards, including sustained inappropriate behavior.

**Consequence**: A temporary ban from any sort of interaction or public communication with the community for a specified period of time. No public or private interaction with the people involved, including unsolicited interaction with those enforcing the Code of Conduct, is allowed during this period. Violating these terms may lead to a permanent ban.

### 4. Permanent Ban

**Community Impact**: Demonstrating a pattern of violation of community standards, including sustained inappropriate behavior, harassment of an individual, or aggression toward or disparagement of classes of individuals.

**Consequence**: A permanent ban from any sort of public interaction within the community.

## Attribution

This Code of Conduct is adapted from the [Contributor Covenant][homepage], version 2.1, available at [https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html][v2.1].

Community Impact Guidelines were inspired by [Mozilla's code of conduct enforcement ladder][Mozilla CoC].

For answers to common questions about this code of conduct, see the FAQ at [https://www.contributor-covenant.org/faq][FAQ]. Translations are available at [https://www.contributor-covenant.org/translations][translations].

# Contributing to Mixdog

Thanks for helping make Mixdog better. Bug reports, reproductions, and root-cause
analysis are as valuable as code. Everyone taking part follows our
[Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).

## Every change starts with an issue

**Bug fixes and features from an outside contributor must link an issue.**
Small changes — typo and wording fixes, documentation, and small type or
formatting fixes that don't change behavior — can go straight to a pull
request. Maintainers and automated dependency updates are always exempt.

1. Search [open and closed issues](https://github.com/tribgames/mixdog/issues?q=is%3Aissue)
   and [pull requests](https://github.com/tribgames/mixdog/pulls?q=is%3Apr) first.
   If one already covers your problem, add what you know there instead.
2. Open an issue with the bug or feature form and describe the problem.
3. For a feature, wait for a maintainer to confirm the issue before you write
   code; pull requests for unconfirmed features may be closed. A bug fix with
   a clear reproduction need not wait.
4. Open your pull request and write `Fixes #123` (or `Refs #123`) in its
   description. For bug fixes and features a check requires that link; docs,
   refactors, and the small changes above are exempt. A pull request that
   changes only documentation passes by its files; for any other small change,
   a maintainer adds the `small-change` label, which passes the check. The
   check only sees the link; a maintainer confirms the issue.

## What we merge

- **One problem per pull request.** Unrelated fixes, refactors, and formatting
  go in separate pull requests. Several small test fixes for the same cause go
  in one pull request, not one each.
- **A test that fails before your change and passes after it.** Changes
  without such a test are not merged unless a test is genuinely impossible;
  then explain how you verified it.
- **The smallest change that fixes the problem.** Extra abstraction, defensive
  branches for cases nobody hits, and broad rewrites are not merged.
- **Land one pull request before opening the next.** Don't open many at once;
  submit them in your order of preference and wait for each to land. If you
  must have several open, keep it to a handful so reviews don't pile up.

## AI-assisted work

Using AI tools is fine, but you are responsible for the final code:
understand the direction and logic of your change well enough to explain it,
and run it yourself before opening the pull request. Write the issue and the
pull request description briefly, in your own words; walls of generated text
may be ignored, and submissions that obviously skip your own review are closed.

## Before you open a pull request

While you work, `npm test -- --changed` (and the same after
`npm test --prefix apps/desktop`) runs only the tests your edits reach. Run the
full commands below once, at the end:

```sh
npm test
npm test --prefix apps/desktop
npm run typecheck --prefix apps/desktop
```

For visible changes, attach before/after screenshots or a short recording.

## Security

Do not report vulnerabilities in public issues. Follow the
[security policy](SECURITY.md).
